mechanism_narrative: A monotone four-week recovery in WORKPLACES mobility (-23.3 to -18.4) signals that commuting routines are re-forming, which restores weekday footfall in retail corridors and pushes mean RETAIL_REC higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -23.3 at t-3w to -18.4 at t-0w in four consecutive steps
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or below its last-28-day mean while WORKPLACES continues to rise toward baseline.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen every week (2.9 to 5.1), showing that time shifted into the home is still accumulating; this home-confinement habit substitutes directly for discretionary out-of-home spending, so RETAIL_REC declines further over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL increased every week from 2.9 to 5.1 while RETAIL_REC fell from -14.7 to -17.7
regime_hint: steady-state confinement with voluntary stay-at-home behavior
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its last-28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL keeps rising week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT broke out of a three-week plateau near -22 and dropped to -24.0 at t-0w; once transit use steps down past that level, non-essential trips are cut first, and RETAIL_REC follows transit lower within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by more than 1.5 points week-on-week and closes below -23.0
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -22.0 at t-1w to -24.0 at t-0w, the largest weekly drop in the window
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT closes below -23.0, mean RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is higher than in weeks where TRANSIT stays above -22.5.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS activity collapsed from 35.0 to 12.9 across the window, marking the end of the outdoor-activity season; as outdoor leisure options close down, discretionary spending is re-routed indoors toward retail and recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 15 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 35.0 at t-3w to 12.9 at t-0w, a 22-point decline
regime_hint: indoor-season transition with PARKS trending down toward baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is flat or lower while PARKS remains below 15.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of rising RESIDENTIAL (2.9 to 5.1) and falling TRANSIT (-22.0 to -24.0) is a confinement signature: trips that were previously chained through transit are replaced by staying home, removing the trip chains that feed retail-and-recreation visits.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises week-on-week while TRANSIT falls week-on-week in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:in the t-1w to t-0w step RESIDENTIAL rose 4.4 to 5.1 while TRANSIT fell -22.0 to -24.0
regime_hint: tightening restrictions with active stay-at-home substitution
failure_condition: In weeks showing the joint RESIDENTIAL-up/TRANSIT-down signature, RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days rises above its value in the week the signature appears.

mechanism_narrative: Under a tightening-restriction regime, GROCERY_PHARM holds near -7 while RETAIL_REC sinks to -17.7, confirming that only essential categories remain tolerated; as long as the essential/non-essential gap widens, RETAIL_REC keeps falling over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: the spread (GROCERY_PHARM minus RETAIL_REC) widens by more than 1.0 point week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell to -17.7 while GROCERY_PHARM stayed in the -6.0 to -7.4 band, widening the gap to about 10 points
regime_hint: tightening restrictions that separate essential from non-essential activity
failure_condition: The GROCERY_PHARM-to-RETAIL_REC spread widens but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or above its prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES recovery (-18.4) together with still-rising RESIDENTIAL (5.1) implies a hybrid pattern where commuting returns only partially while home-based time keeps expanding; the residential expansion dominates leisure allocation, so net RETAIL_REC is lower over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises by at least 0.5 points in the same week WORKPLACES rises by less than 2.0 points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 4.9 points over four weeks while RESIDENTIAL rose 2.2 points and RETAIL_REC fell 3.0 points
regime_hint: partial reopening with persistent voluntary home-stay
failure_condition: When RESIDENTIAL outpaces WORKPLACES gains, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS crossing down through the 15 level in a single week removes the outdoor-mobility buffer that had absorbed discretionary trips; with that outlet gone, overall trip-making contracts and RETAIL_REC falls within one week of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: PARKS drops more than 10 points in a single week and closes below 15
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 14.8 points from 26.1 at t-2w to 11.3 at t-1w, and TRANSIT subsequently fell to -24.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: In the week after a PARKS drop of more than 10 points below 15, RETAIL_REC is equal to or higher than in the week of the drop.
